strategy.audience: Non-technical small-business leader, AI level 0-6 of 10 (POSITIONING.md §4): an owner, operations lead or team lead in a 5-50 person company who is responsible for one repeated process and has tried ChatGPT but has no repeatable way of using it at work. Specifically anyone who quotes a figure that is calculated somewhere else - a margin, a price, a stock count, a headline number in a monthly report.
strategy.concept: One figure in our own files has two correct values, fourteen times and one point nine times, because one calculation leaves the item out of its own comparison and the other leaves it in - and on a creator whose plays fall into two clumps with nothing between them, that alone moves the yardstick nearly eightfold. We acted on the bigger one.

filter.ai_boundary: The machine can recompute the figure wherever it appears and flag the moment two places disagree. Deciding which definition is the authoritative one is a human decision, and it has to be written down once rather than re-argued each month.
filter.friction: Both versions are defensible and both are quoted by people who trust them, so the disagreement is invisible until a decision has already been made on whichever one was nearer to hand. Reviewing harder does not find it, because neither number is wrong.
filter.next_action: Take the figure you quote most often, find the second place it is worked out, and write down which of the two is authoritative.
filter.process: Producing a recurring figure that other people act on - the margin in the monthly pack, the headline number in a report, a price, a stock count - where the figure is worked out in one system and quoted in another.

strategy.objective: Send the viewer looking for the second place their most-quoted figure is worked out, by showing a fourteen-fold difference that survived a review inside our own files.
strategy.promise: One page that stops the same figure meaning two things in two systems.
strategy.rationale: No reel in the 266-reel corpus corrects its own number: 36 use numbers as proof and every one presents the number as settled. The references supply shape only - an exact figure spoken over the record it describes (DaGTeJNN1GR), one named thing per step with no connective tissue (DUJYKENjZc5), the screen carrying the payoff while the face carries only the interpretation (DYC-x8DogOI), and, as a negative example, a save bought entirely by withholding the artefact (DVtgbY8Av6A), which we invert by publishing it.

title: The same number in two places

traceability.evidence_summary: One of our 23 drafted planning cards carried a headline figure of 14.4 times normal. The same item recomputed against all twelve of that author's reels in our files is 1.87 times normal, and it sits seventh of the twelve, at the 54th percentile, outlier_status NORMAL. Both figures come from the same twelve reels in the same snapshot and differ only by whether the item is inside its own comparison: 19 624 is the middle of the other eleven, 151 569.5 the middle of all twelve. It moves that far because the creator's plays fall into two clumps - six from 7 402 to 19 624, six from 283 515 to 768 383 - with the middle sitting in the empty stretch. Both figures reproduce from data/radar.db. The four references contribute shape only: an exact figure spoken over the thing it describes (DaGTeJNN1GR, 30.2 shares/1k, robust_z 3.41), one named thing per step (DUJYKENjZc5, 36.6 shares/1k), the screen carrying the payoff and the face only the interpretation (DYC-x8DogOI, 59.9 saves/1k) and, inverted, a save bought by withholding the artefact (DVtgbY8Av6A, 57.3 saves/1k).
traceability.original_synthesis: No reel in the 266-reel corpus corrects its own number - 36 use numbers as proof and every one presents the number as settled. The wrong figure, the right figure, the twelve rows behind both and the decision taken on the larger one are ours and dated. The script deliberately contains no statistical vocabulary: the mechanism is delivered as two receipts for the same job with different totals, and the artefact we hand over is a one-page definition sheet published in the caption rather than gated behind a comment.
traceability.why_better_than_generic: A generic AI script would warn that 'AI can hallucinate numbers' and move on. Nothing hallucinated here: both figures are arithmetically correct on the same twelve rows, which is the whole point and the reason reviewing harder does not catch it. This reel names the exact item, both middles, the gap in the data that makes them seven times apart, and the one-line rule that closes it - and it does so without using the words median, baseline or percentile once.
